answer: Cost-to-Coordinate Escrow: each identity must post a deposit that scales with the number of distinct counterparties it transacts with in a rolling window. A sybil cluster trying to look organic must create genuine transaction ripple across many unrelated parties, and each new edge pulls fresh escrow from that identity, so breadth itself becomes expensive. A cheap kernel of fake accounts can’t fake wide interaction without paying per-connection locked capital that honest narrow users never owe. The grove of real participants stays cheap because their coordination is sparse and stable.
